Hi [USER] - thanks for reaching out!
If the app you are referencing is based on the code [here](https://github.com/biswa2026/Agentic/blob/main/RAG_Infobot_tool_Agentic.py) - you may be reaching usage limits because if scraping fails, `db_ready` remains `False`, and `st.rerun()` gets called repeatedly in an infinite loop. This would rapidly consume CPU cycles and memory.
Rebooting your app will help temporarily, but for a longer term solution the app will likely need some refactoring - some tips in this forum [post](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/common-app-problems-resource-limits/16969).

Hello Streamlit Support Team,

I am writing to request assistance regarding an issue with my Streamlit Community Cloud account.

When I try to log in to Streamlit Cloud, I consistently receive the following error message:

“Huh. This isn’t supposed to happen.
Error: Your account has exceeded the fair-use limits and was blocked by the system.
Code: 403”

At the moment, I am unable to log in to Streamlit Cloud or access my deployed apps at all.

This happened while I was developing and testing an app. The app itself is not resource-intensive, but it is possible that during development I unintentionally caused excessive reruns or repeated function calls (for example, due to state handling or rerun logic). If so, this was unintentional, and I am happy to refactor the app to fully comply with the fair-use policy once access is restored.

I would appreciate it if you could please review my account and let me know:

* Whether the block can be lifted, and
* If there is any specific guidance I should follow to prevent this from happening again.

Details:

* GitHub username: jjm1128jjm-ctrl
* Streamlit account email: [EMAIL]
* App URL (if applicable): jjm-tensile.streamlit.app

Thank you very much for your time and support.
I appreciate any help you can provide.

Kind regards,
Jeon Jaemin
